title: TAP bug report data block
description: The one machine-readable block inside a bug report: the single fenced JSON document that `submit-a-bug` writes and `submit-a-fix` reads (req-dev-bugreport-shape-1, req-dev-bugreport-shape-3). This file is the only place the report's fields are defined; neither skill restates them, and tap/tests/test_bug_report.py fails when a field here is written by one side and not read by the other. Version 0 carries no dataset and no value from the reporter's instance: the failing shape is types, field names and value forms, never values (req-dev-bugreport-synthetic-7).

description.description: What this document is, in a sentence: the machine-readable block of a TAP bug report. Present because every JSON structure carries a description at its top level and on each key.

schema_version.description: Version of this report shape. 0 means the report carries no synthetic dataset (req-dev-bugreport-synthetic-7). A later version that adds a GRIFT document changes this number and this file together.

target_repository.description: The repository that owns the failing code, as owner/name: read from the install's boot record for a plugin, `unified-systems-com/tap` for core or an unattributed failure (req-dev-bugreport-route-2).

title.description: The issue title: one line naming the symptom in TAP's own vocabulary (a plugin slug, a model or field name, an error class), never a value from the reporter's instance.

versions.description: The versions and commits the failure was seen at; `submit-a-fix` reproduces at these commits and again at main (req-dev-bugfix-reproduce-2).

description.description: What this object holds: the TAP and plugin versions of the reporter's install.

tap_version.description: The TAP core version or image tag the reporter runs, from the running install and never from an env file.

tap_commit.description: The core commit, when the reporter runs from a git checkout; null when only a release or image tag is known.

profile_kind.description: The boot profile's `profile_kind`, one of the environment allowlist's fixed sources (req-dev-bugreport-environment).

plugins.description: Every installed plugin from the boot record. A plugin sourced outside unified-systems-com appears only as third-party with its rev; its slug and repository are never written (req-dev-bugreport-environment).

third_party.description: True when the plugin's source URL is outside unified-systems-com; its slug is then null because the slug and repository may be private.

slug.description: The plugin slug for a unified-systems-com plugin; null for a third-party plugin.

rev.description: The `rev` the boot record installed the plugin at (a tag or ref).

commit.description: The `commit` the boot record names for a unified-systems-com plugin; null for a third-party plugin.

failing_operation.description: The operation that fails, in words and TAP vocabulary: a management command, a page or API route, a collector name, a Gryphon clause. No instance values.

failing_shape.description: The shape that fails: which node and edge types, which fields, which relationships, as types, field names, cardinalities and value forms. Never values (req-dev-bugreport-synthetic-1, -7).

description.description: What this object holds: the failing shape, without values.

node_types.description: Slugs of the node types involved.

edge_types.description: Slugs of the edge types involved.

cardinalities.description: Relationship counts that matter, as words, for example `one repository, many packages`.

fields.description: Each field in the shape with its classification, the table the reporter reviewed (req-dev-bugreport-synthetic-2, -3).

type.description: The node or edge type slug the field belongs to.

field.description: The field name as the published schema spells it.

form.description: The value's form, never the value: for example `uuid`, `ipv4 address`, `email`, `free text`, `non-negative integer`.

sensitive.description: True when a real value would identify the reporter, their organisation, infrastructure or a person, or would grant access. A field with no published description is always true (req-dev-bugreport-synthetic-3).

judgement.description: Why the field was judged as it was, quoting the schema's own description, or stating that none is published (a schema gap).

steps.description: The ordered steps that reproduce the failure, each in the reporter's words or TAP vocabulary, with no instance values.

summary.description: The expected result in words, typed by the reporter or passed through the tripwire.

count.description: The expected row, node or message count where the result is a count; null otherwise.

summary.description: The actual result in words: an error class and message template with its values removed, or what was seen.

count.description: The actual row, node or message count where the result is a count; null otherwise.

synthetic_data.description: Whether the report carries a synthetic dataset and whether it reproduced. Version 0 carries none (req-dev-bugreport-synthetic-7).

included.description: Always false in version 0: no GRIFT document and no dataset travel with the report.

reproduced.description: Always false in version 0: with no dataset there is nothing that reproduced on synthetic data, and the disclosure line says so.

environment.description: Environment facts drawn only from the fixed allowlist of sources (req-dev-bugreport-environment).

description.description: What this object holds: the environment allowlist's facts.

run_mode.description: How TAP is being run: the bug issue form's own dropdown.

health_output.description: The text `manage.py health` printed, after it passed the tripwire; null when not attached.

anything_else.description: Free text the reporter chose to add. It passes the tripwire like everything else (req-dev-bugreport-environment).
